card.name: Verbs and endings in all-caps warnings
card.fires_on: Small grammar pieces in all-capitals label warnings, such as plural S, IS, TO, BE, MADE, after a drug or patient noun. Also fires on an opening parenthesis before e.g. in symptom lists.

modes.label: Plural ending in caps
modes.description: The final S of a plural noun like PATIENTS or DRUGS in an all-caps warning sentence.
modes.example: ATORVASTATIN SHOULD BE ADMINISTERED TO WOMEN OF CHILDBEARING AGE ONLY WHEN SUCH PATIENT<<S>> ARE HIGHLY UNLIKELY TO CONCE

modes.label: Helper verbs in caps
modes.description: Short helper words like IS, TO, BE, MADE or CANNOT inside an all-caps instruction.
modes.example: INTRAVENOUS INJECTION SHOULD BE<< MADE>> SLOWLY AND WITH REPEATED

modes.label: Parenthesis before e.g.
modes.description: An opening bracket that introduces examples in a symptom list.

card.writes: It suppresses sur- word starts and mildly favors words like surrounded or enclosed, with no clear link to the text.
card.plain: It lights up on small connecting words and endings inside shouted all-capital label warnings.
